solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Instrument in vessel about to go on fire

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them

indicators.note: about signals that the vessel word is turned round

parts.note: a tub is a vessel for holding liquid

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is stowed in a ship that is about to catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but here it is a tub, which 'about' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackbut is an early form of trombone, a brass musical instrument.

clue.text: Formally acknowledged something played entering grave

indicators.note: entering signals one piece going inside the word for grave

parts.note: grave means serious or sad
a lute is an instrument, something one plays

explanation.surface: A tune played at a solemn graveside formally honours someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To salute is to greet or acknowledge with a formal gesture.

clue.text: Made a deal and embraced, having taken up little time

indicators.note: having taken signals that the embracing word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: embraced in the sense of included, comprised

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the short time word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a little time

explanation.surface: Two people made a deal and hugged after a brief pause.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the short time backwards; 'embraced' means included, not hugged.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise is to settle a dispute by mutual concession, striking a deal.

clue.text: Renamed city business qualification lad possesses

indicators.note: possesses signals that the lad word holds the qualification inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
MBA is a Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: A young man in a renamed city has an MBA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city of Bombay was officially renamed Mumbai in 1995.

clue.text: Having several sides subsequently participating in test

indicators.note: participating in signals one piece being placed within the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test
subsequently means later

explanation.surface: A multi-sided matter later becomes part of an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilateral describes something with three sides or three parties, so more than two.

clue.text: Dance classes for poet and priest

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
kins are families or classes of related people

explanation.surface: Dance lessons are offered to a clergyman who writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerard Manley Hopkins was a Victorian poet who was also a Jesuit priest.

clue.text: African university given superior temporary accommodation

indicators.note: in a down clue, given superior means the shelter word is placed above the university letter

parts.note: a hut is a simple, temporary shelter

explanation.surface: An African university is provided with prefab huts for its buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hutu are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a Hutu is an African.

clue.text: Attack malevolent little creature that's got rid of black mammal

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, attack

indicators.note: got rid of signals the black letter being dropped from the creature

parts.note: a goblin is a mischievous little sprite
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a nasty little imp that has done away with a dark thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's got rid of' removes B from GOBLIN, leaving GOLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The pangolin is a scaly anteater, a mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Boozer liked being heard

indicators.note: being heard signals a word that sounds like the one for liked

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular or liked

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker enjoyed being listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is British slang for a pub, not a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A boozer is British slang for a pub, and an inn is a pub.

clue.text: What could be nastier component of fat

indicators.note: could be signals the letters of nastier rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Asks what might be the more unpleasant part of fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearin is a glyceride found in animal fats, used in candles and soap.

clue.text: Escape, having left before noon

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Someone escaped, having left during the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: On the lam is American slang for fleeing; lam as a noun is a hasty escape.

clue.text: Number joining party for Africans in US state care

indicators.note: in signals the number and party being placed inside the state

parts.note: Maine is a US state
ten is a number
the ANC is the African National Congress, a South African party

explanation.surface: An African political party sets up a care programme in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like the numb thing but is just TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintenance is upkeep, the care given to keep something in good order.

clue.text: Refuse a course of action after shock

indicators.note: after places the shock word before the rest

parts.note: a turn is a sudden shock, as in giving someone a turn
a way is a method or course of action

explanation.surface: Someone declines a plan after a nasty fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn away is to reject or refuse admission to someone.

clue.text: Cold criminal heading off to be a fellow down under

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: heading off signals that the first letter of the criminal is dropped

parts.note: a robber is a criminal

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted crook absconds to Australia to become one of the blokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobber is Australian slang for a mate, a pal or fellow.

clue.text: Encouraging action at end of round in fight

indicators.note: in signals the bell action placed inside the fight word

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match, a fight
a bell is rung to end each boxing round, so ringing

explanation.surface: Cheering on a boxer as the bell sounds at the end of a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing someone out is encouraging them to be more confident and sociable.

clue.text: Roughly what we do as presents are handed out?

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning approximately, within a small margin

definitions.text: what we do as presents are handed out?
definitions.meaning: at a gift exchange we hand over presents and receive them

explanation.surface: Approximately describes what happens when gifts go round.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means approximately; read literally it is handing over and receiving gifts.

clue.text: What was busted in war with power — having a bit of water!

parts.note: German dams were breached in the Dambusters raid of the Second World War
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A wartime target burst open with great force, releasing water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dambusters were the RAF squadron that breached German dams in 1943.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damp is slightly wet, holding a little moisture.

clue.text: Element of clue, one I'd fit in deviously

indicators.note: deviously signals the letters of one I'd fit in being twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A setter slyly slots in a part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Every cryptic clue contains a definition part alongside its wordplay.

clue.text: Like many a tune coming from evil Hollywood star

parts.note: sin is evil, wrongdoing
Clark Gable was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A popular melody comes from a wicked film star.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that can be sung easily, which applies to most melodies.

clue.text: Players are outside entrance getting rebukes

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show

indicators.note: outside signals the verb wrapping around the entrance word

parts.note: with the players taken as one cast, are becomes is
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Actors waiting outside the stage door are told off.
explanation.walkthrough: A cast is a singular noun, so the clue's plural verb stands for the singular one.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to reprimand severely, so castigates means rebukes.

clue.text: Picks confectionery treats: second about to go

indicators.note: to go signals that letter being removed

parts.note: choc ices are chocolate-coated ice cream bars
about gives c, the abbreviation of circa

explanation.surface: Someone selects sweets and ice creams, but one is about to be taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: Choc ices are British chocolate-coated ice creams; 'second' says it is their second C that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Picks as a plural noun means selections, things chosen.

clue.text: Last one of the tribe to give utterance of surprise

indicators.note: last one of picks the final letter of the word the

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: The final member of a tribe lets out a cry of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old-fashioned exclamation, a mild oath expressing surprise.

clue.text: Resident embarrassed, upset about non-mains water supply

indicators.note: about signals the reversed colour going around the water source
upset in a down clue turns the colour word upside down, backwards

parts.note: being embarrassed makes one red in the face
a well supplies water not drawn from the mains

explanation.surface: A householder is embarrassed and upset about a private water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the colour word upside down, giving DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller is someone who lives somewhere, an inhabitant.

clue.text: Approach a planet without second source of energy

indicators.note: without signals dropping the second abbreviation from the planet

parts.note: Venus is a planet

indicators.note: source of picks the first letter of energy

explanation.surface: A planet is approached without a source of power.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a road leading up to a house, an approach; figuratively a way in.

clue.text: Wrongly gaoled when one could be in a home?

definitions.text: when one could be in a home?
definitions.note: a time of life rather than a noun for a person

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters of gaoled put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly imprisoned when they might be in a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaoled' is the British spelling of jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly people may live in a retirement or care home in their later years.

clue.text: A knight leaving birthplace somewhere in France

indicators.note: leaving signals those letters going out of the origin word

parts.note: provenance is a place of origin
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight departs from his home town for a place in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Provence is a region in the south-east of France.

clue.text: Cricketer accumulating runs, a spoilt youngster?

indicators.note: accumulating signals the cricketer taking the runs inside

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A young cricketer piles up runs and becomes spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is a badly behaved, spoilt child.

clue.text: PM put down by house of legislature

indicators.note: by places the house word beside the past participle

parts.note: a chamber is a house of a legislature
lain is the past participle of lie, laid down

explanation.surface: A prime minister is defeated by a parliamentary house.
explanation.definitionFit: Neville Chamberlain was British Prime Minister from 1937 to 1940.

clue.text: Beautiful female lacking expression

indicators.note: lacking signals the female letter being taken out

parts.note: fair means beautiful

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman has a blank face.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a look or manner one shows, an outward expression.

clue.text: Extract sulphur out of earth

indicators.note: out of signals the sulphur symbol being removed

parts.note: soil is earth
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Instructions to take sulphur out of the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils are often extracted from plants, such as olive oil pressed from fruit.

clue.text: Artists taken aback by male painter noted for portraits

indicators.note: taken aback signals the artists' letters read backwards

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, artists
a gent is a man, a male

explanation.surface: Fellow artists are startled by a man known for painting portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was a leading society portraitist around 1900.

clue.text: Horse has calm expression after losing its tail

parts.note: even means calm, as in an even temper

indicators.note: losing its tail signals that the last letter of the expression is dropped

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

explanation.surface: A horse keeps a calm look after its tail is docked.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse trained for eventing, the equestrian three-day contest.
